methodology.title: How we calculate
methodology.intro: WheelWise does not guess. Every amount on the site comes from public data and an open cost model. This page says where the numbers come from and where their precision ends.

prices.heading: Car prices are indicative
paragraphs: WheelWise shows what owning a new car costs: in złoty, for drivers in Poland. We do not sell cars and we do not mediate purchases.
The car catalogue and prices come from ADEME Car Labelling, an open dataset run by a French government agency. They are list prices of new cars in France.

We convert the price to złoty: the French price in euro times the NBP mid euro rate, with French VAT of 20% replaced by Polish VAT of 23%, rounded to 100 zł. That is why every price is marked “indicative price” and carries the date of the price list.

The price at a Polish dealer may differ from the one shown by several percent or more, because manufacturers set prices country by country. The range of models and versions is the French one, so some cars sold in Poland are missing. The French ecological bonus and malus are not included in the prices.
One car is a model in one body type, with one powertrain, one gearbox and one power figure. From each such group we show the cheapest version.

Car names are the commercial descriptions of the source, unchanged. Versions that differ in drive (2WD / 4WD), battery size, number of seats or equipment are shown as one car at the price of the cheapest of them; the others cost more.

costs.heading: What the cost is made of
paragraphs: The total cost is the sum of six categories. The purchase price is not added: depreciation stands in for it, the part of the price you will not get back when you sell. We assume a cash purchase.
list: Depreciation: the price minus the estimated value of the car after the chosen period. The value depends on the number of years, mileage, powertrain and make.

Fuel and energy: WLTP consumption times your mileage and the current price of fuel (petrol, diesel, LPG) or electricity. Electric cars are charged at home, at the household electricity price. Hybrids run on petrol, and for plug-in hybrids we count both fuel and electricity.
Insurance: third-party (OC) or comprehensive (OC + AC) cover, estimated from the driver’s age and the power and value of the car, or the premium you enter yourself.
Servicing: inspections and scheduled service. It depends on the make and mileage and is lower for electric cars.
Parts and wear: tyres, brakes and other wear parts. They depend on mileage, the size of the car and the make.
Fees: registration of a new car (160 zł) and periodic roadworthiness tests (149 zł, 245 zł for LPG cars) that fall before the end of the ownership period.
after: We do not include loans, leasing, parking, tolls, fines, washing or tyre storage.

estimates.heading: What the ≈ sign means
paragraphs: No open data exists per model for depreciation, insurance, servicing and parts. We calculate them with a model whose parameters follow published market averages. Each such amount is preceded by the ≈ sign.
WLTP consumption is usually lower than in everyday driving, plug-in hybrids especially. The real fuel cost will tend to be higher than shown.

power.heading: Power of electric and hybrid cars
paragraphs: For petrol, diesel and LPG cars the source gives the maximum engine power, and that is what we show.

For hybrids and plug-in hybrids the source gives the power of the combustion engine only. The power of the whole system, electric motor included, is higher, but the data does not contain it. That is why these cars are labelled “combustion engine power”.

For electric cars the data has no maximum power. We show the highest figure the source gives. For most models this is the rated (continuous) power, clearly lower than the peak power in the manufacturer’s brochure: the Tesla Model 3 is listed at 88 kW. That is why electric cars are labelled “power per source data”. The figure also has a small effect on the insurance estimate.

income.heading: The income scale
paragraphs: The scale shows the net monthly income (take-home pay) at which the total cost of the car, depreciation included, takes a given share of the budget. It follows the 20/4/10 rule and common guidance from financial advisers. Amounts are rounded to 100 zł, and the yearly view is 12 times the monthly amount.
list: comfortable: the car takes up to 10% of income

freshness.heading: How often the data is refreshed
paragraphs: Once a day we check every source. Each publishes at its own pace, which is why prices carry their date.
The date next to a car price (“Price list of”) is the day the source last updated its data, not the day we checked it. The date of our last check is in the footer of the page.
